name: Leatherworker
summary: A Universal World Class any character may take regardless of their class. It levels through active use (every step at the tanner's beam and the vat), opening methods and rarer hides at levels 1 to 3. Past level 3 the levels never stop, and each one grants two perks: potency, hardening, quality or yield.
_ruling_2026_10_05_note: The owner's leatherworking revamp (docs/leatherworking-questions.md, nine rounds answered 2026-10-05, and the plan's open points answered 2026-10-08; docs/leatherworking-revamp-plan.md §7, §8, §10, §11, §17). Three unlock levels replace five: level 1 is field work on common and uncommon hides (Salt, Flense, Tan by brain or as rawhide, Cut, Stitch, Harden, Assemble, Grade); level 2 the tannery's work and rare and exotic hides (bark, alum and mineral tannages, Curry, Tool, Dye, Laminate); level 3 legendary hides and the planar tannages. Harden is a level-1 method because the owner put 'a small kettle' in the field kit (answer 3, 2026-10-08): 'plain leather armour is therefore makeable at level 1 in the field'. Skin became the cross-craft harvest (rules/harvest.py, lane C), Cure became Salt (which really takes salt), Oil folded into Curry, and Line became the lining piece at Assemble. The level 4 and 5 rows, the `legendary-hide` milestone and its deed are gone. Old saves keep their level: an old Leatherworker 4 holds one pair of perk picks, an old 5 two (`worldclass.migrate_leatherworker`).
_thresholds_note: Mastery to reach levels 2 and 3; every level after that is priced by `endless`. 25 and 65 are the Herbalist's and the Blacksmith's numbers on purpose: the crafts are meant to pace the same.
_endless_note: Levels past the written table (plan §17.2; the forge's four, Yield moved to the harvest, owner Q6.3). Leaving level 3 costs `base` and each level after it `step` more (50, 60, 70...). Each endless level banks `picks_per_level` picks; the same perk may be taken twice. Potency adds to the multiplier on the bonus modifiers of everything made, hardening takes that fraction off the negative modifiers (multiplied with the per-level cut), quality raises the ceiling by that many steps, and yield is read at the HARVEST (lane C): the chance per hide taken of more hide units, rolled and shown. The bench reads no yield.
_ceiling_note: `ceiling` is the highest quality index a level's hands can reach (0 Crude, 1 Sound, 2 Fine, 3 Superior, 4 Flawless), the forge's table (plan §17.3). Superior or better is masterwork. Each Quality perk adds one past Flawless.

tools: leatherworker's field kit: skinning knife, fleshing beam, round knife, awl and needles, mallet, a small kettle
levels.note: Field work on common and uncommon hides: salt a green hide before it spoils, flense it, tan it with brain or dry it as rawhide, cut and stitch it, boil bark-tanned panels hard in the kit's small kettle, and lace the pieces into a suit, a madu or a cloak.
The tannery's work: bark tanning in a vat for weeks, alum tawing, mineral tanning, currying, tooling, dyeing and laminating two leathers into one. Rare and exotic hides; Superior work is masterwork.
Legendary hides, dragonhide among them, and the planar tannages: dragonblood, wyrm gall, the Styx mordant.

method_descriptions.salt: Rubs curing salt into a green hide. A salted hide keeps for weeks instead of rotting in two days, which buys the time to reach a beam or a vat.
method_descriptions.flense: Scrapes the flesh and fat off the inside of a hide over the beam, hair on for a fur, off for leather. A thick hide is limed in a tannery's pit for days before the hair and flesh will come away.
method_descriptions.tan: Turns a fleshed hide into leather or fur. Brain tanning is a day's work at the kit; alum tawing takes a week in a sealed bag; bark, mineral and planar tannages sit in a tannery's vat for days or weeks while you go about your business. With no tannin at all the hide is stretched and dried as rawhide.
method_descriptions.curry: Works oil and tallow into tanned leather until it is supple and sheds water. A soft good needs it before it can be Superior work.
method_descriptions.cut: Cuts panels to a pattern, a lacing set or a grip strip, combining hides of one kind and grade until there is enough.
method_descriptions.stitch: Sews cut panels into a body or a lining with thread or sinew.
method_descriptions.harden: Cuir bouilli: soaks bark-tanned panels and works them in hot water until they set hard. The kit's small kettle does it for common and uncommon hides; rarer ones want a tannery's hardening kettle. Brain, alum and mineral leather will not harden.
method_descriptions.tool: Stamps and carves the leather's face while it is cased. Required for Flawless work.
method_descriptions.dye: Colours a piece. Mordant salts fix the colour; without them it runs in the first soaking.
method_descriptions.laminate: Glues and stitches two leathers of one hide and one tannage into one heavier leather: every modifier half as strong again, the drawbacks too.
method_descriptions.assemble: Joins a body, its fastenings and a lining into the finished suit, shield or worn good, or into a base the forge finishes.
method_descriptions.grade: Flexes and reads a scrap of a material: one property it gives and one it costs.

_method_help_note: The structured half of a method's tooltip: `does` is the mechanical effect, `needs` what must be on the bench, `for` what a player reaches for it to do. Every method in the level table has an entry; tests/test_benches.py asserts the two sets match.

salt.does: Stops a green hide's 48-hour clock for six weeks.
salt.needs: A green or fleshed hide that is not yet salted, and one measure of curing salt for each hide unit.
salt.for: Buying time between the kill and the beam.

flense.does: Turns a green or salted hide into a pelt ready to tan. A thick hide waits three days in a tannery's lime pit.
flense.needs: A hide that has not spoiled. A thick hide needs a tannery.
flense.for: Nothing can be tanned until it is fleshed.

tan.does: Makes leather or fur (or rawhide with no tannin). The tannin decides the wait, where it happens and whether the leather can later be hardened, and its working traits move the quality ceiling.
tan.needs: A pelt and a tannin within one tier of the hide, one measure a hide unit. Bark, mineral and planar tannins need a tannery's vat.

curry.does: Dresses tanned leather. A soft body must be curried before Assemble can reach Superior.
curry.needs: Tanned leather or fur, and an oil.

cut.does: Cuts panels for a pattern's body or lining, a lacing set, or a grip. Hides of one kind and grade combine; what is left over goes back on the rack.
cut.needs: Tanned leather, fur or rawhide, enough hide units for the pattern.

stitch.does: Sews panels into a body or a lining.
stitch.for: Every soft body and every lining.

harden.does: Boils bark- or planar-tanned panels into hardened plates (cuir bouilli), the body of leather armour, lamellar and the madu.
harden.needs: Panels cut for a plated pattern, bark or planar tanned. The kit's kettle hardens common and uncommon hides; rare and up need a tannery.
harden.for: Leather armour, which the book says is boiled.

tool.does: Tools the leather's face. Assemble cannot reach Flawless without a tooled body.
tool.needs: A tanned piece, and a wax if you have one.

dye.does: Colours a piece; with mordant salts the colour is fast.
dye.needs: A tanned piece and a dye.

laminate.does: Two leathers of one hide, grade and tannage become one, a strengthening pass: every modifier x1.5.

assemble.does: Makes the finished item. Suits and shields are the book's Craft DC (10 + armour bonus), worn and carried goods DC 10; aiming for masterwork is DC 20 unless the hide is masterwork by nature.
assemble.needs: A body cut for the pattern (stitched panels, or hardened plates for leather armour, lamellar and the madu), fastenings for a suit or shield, and a lining if you want one.
assemble.for: Armour, shields, cloaks, boots and bags.

grade.does: Reveals one benefit and one drawback of a material.
grade.needs: A field kit or a tannery, and a scrap of the material: a quarter unit of hide, or one measure of a supply.
grade.for: Knowing what a hide will do before you build with it.

_bench_note: The leather bench's rule rows (docs/leatherworking-revamp-plan.md §5.5, §6, §7, §8, §10, §11, §13; contracts §7), read by rules/leatherworker.py. Every number the plan marks proposed lives here so it tunes without a code change. `where` is `kit` (the field kit or a tannery) or `tannery`. `bulk` methods take a batch: one roll and one game for the stack. `minutes` is per hide unit where `per_unit` is true, else per piece. `tuning`: `difficulty` is the game's base, raised by `rarity_step` per band above common (rarer hides narrow the window, the forge's Giants' Foundry rule), and `band` is the real variable the game shows (docs/leatherworking-prior-art.md §3.9): its unit, the target band, the failing band, where it starts and how fast it drifts.

salt.name: Salt
salt.takes: a green hide and curing salt

tan.name: Tan
tan.takes: a pelt and a tannin (none: rawhide)

curry.name: Curry
curry.takes: tanned leather or fur, and an oil

cut.name: Cut
cut.makes: panels, a lacing set or a grip

tool.name: Tool
tool.takes: a tanned piece, and a wax if you like

dye.name: Dye
dye.takes: a tanned piece, a dye, and mordant salts for a fast colour

assemble.name: Assemble
assemble.takes: a body, fastenings, and a lining if you have one

bench._tannages_note: Plan §8.1 (proposed times). `minutes` is bench time (a flat setup, or per hide unit where `per_unit`); `wait_minutes` is how long it then waits In progress (rules/inprogress.py), `thick_wait_minutes` for a thick hide. `where` is where the wait happens: `kit` travels with you (a brain tan needs no wait at all; rawhide dries and alum ages in the pack), `tannery` sits in a vat at the tannery and is collected there. `hardens`: whether the leather takes Harden (vegetable and planar only; alum softens in water). `vat`: false for work that fills no vat. `shrink_c` is the tannage's shrinkage temperature (prior art §3.9), shown, never a game. A tannin's own `fast_tan` and `slow_tan` traits, and the hide's, scale the wait (`traits`).
bench._units_note: Hide units (plan §5.5, proposed): one Medium hide is one unit, doubling per size; stored in quarters. `products` is what a pattern's body takes for a Medium wearer (a suit's body scales with the wearer's size by `suit_by_size`) and its lining. The book's only printed yield is dragonhide's: one dragon gives a suit for a creature one size smaller, which is exactly two units for a Large dragon.
bench._gates_note: `masterwork_dc` and `masterwork_index` are the book's: a masterwork component is DC 20 (CRB Craft), and Superior (index 3) or better is masterwork, unless the main hide is masterwork by nature (`always_masterwork`, plan §13.4) or `flawless` (Unchained), which waive the DC. `book_dc`: a suit or shield is 10 + its armour bonus, worn and carried goods a typical item, 10. `grade_caps`: the hide grade's cap on any work from it (plan §5.7: grade 1 none, 2 Superior, 3 Fine, 4 Sound). `flawless_needs_tool`: Assemble cannot reach Flawless on an untooled body (plan §7, proposed). `forge_fittings`: fastenings that make a forge suit (steel studs make studded leather), refused at this bench with the reason, because the forge finishes them (owner Q1.3). `fastenings_for`: a pattern that takes only these fastenings.
bench._bought_note: A counter sells a hide tanned, never green (Harvest Parts: a green hide 'cannot be bought or sold in most settlements'; plan §9). Lane D's proposal (docs/leatherworking-review.md): a bought hide is in its document's `sold_as` form, oak-bark tanned (a town tannery's bark tan, so it can be hardened), grade 2, its units by its size.
bench._clock_note: Plan §6: a green hide keeps 48 hours from the harvest (the herbalist's animal clock; a document's own `fresh_hours` wins); a salted one keeps six weeks (FAO, about 15% salt), then the clock runs again. A spoiled hide is scrap: it can still be graded and sold as glue stock, never worked.
bench._traits_note: What the working traits do at the bench (plan §8.1, §14.6; proposed). `time` scales a tannage's wait, `ceiling` moves the quality ceiling of the tannage and everything later made from that leather, `band` scales every game's band and `<method>_band` only that method's. Read off the hide and the tannin in hand.

_old_methods_note: Methods removed 2026-10-05 and what an old recipe naming one maps onto (plan §7). Skin left the bench for the harvest of a carcass (lane C), so it maps onto nothing here.
_portable_note: Where you work is read from the scene (rules/places.py `leather_bench_here`) and the pack (the leatherworker's field kit), never from the player's words (plan §10). The kit works common and uncommon hides anywhere, Harden included (the owner's small kettle, 2026-10-08); a tannery, a town's you pay for by the hour and its vats by the day, or one you found and own, adds the vats (bark, mineral and planar tannages), the lime pit for thick hides and rare-and-up hides. A tannery never refuses a tannage for want of a vat: vats are rented as the work needs (the lead's ruling, 2026-10-08).
_fixed_tools_note: Read now. The 2026-08-25 ruling ('leave these alone until property ownership exists') is retired by plan §10, as the forge retired it for smithies: founded places and their `holds.place.<slug>` effects exist, so a tannery is a place you can own, and the bench asks where you are standing.
